exact_items: Add explicit route validation rules to Contracts_V0.md.
State that invalid route payloads are contract failures, not 'best effort' cases.
Normalize before route construction, not during late destination-specific handling.

Canonical route validation rules are: reject when project_id is missing; reject when no primary selector exists; reject when both subject_id and object_kind/object_id are supplied as competing primary selectors; reject when object_kind is present without object_id; reject when object_id is present without object_kind; reject when inspector_target is present but no object selector exists; reject when tab_id conflicts with target_kind; reject when line or range appears in route_target; reject when per-surface state appears in route_target.
Current docs define plenty of positive rules, but almost no explicit invalid-combination rules.
Without rejection rules, route producers will keep slipping local payload habits into the base contract.
A bounded contract needs rejection rules. Otherwise every bad payload becomes a precedent.
notes: Contracts_V0.md is missing an explicit invalid-combination rejection rules section. This is a structural gap in the owner doc, not a consumer drift issue.

exact_items: Define tab_id as stable page-tab focus only.
Start with the Orchestrator tab family as the first canonical enum set.
Keep panel-subview and shell-tab identities outside the route base contract.
tab_id should stay absent when the destination surface can reveal the target without explicit tab forcing.
The current high-value canonical vocabulary is: Orchestrator: progress, seams, node_graph, evidence, history, ledger
Older docs still blur page tabs, panel subviews, workspace tabs, and browser tabs as if they were one kind of thing.
workspace_tab_id and browser_tab_id remain real shell identities, but they are not canonical route tab_id values.
canonical_replacement_hints: tab_id is stable page-tab focus only; workspace/browser tab ids are shell identities outside route base contract

exact_items: Add scoped-identity resolver rules to Contracts_V0.md.
Keep scoped runtime families object-first and resolver-backed.
Do not add family-specific top-level route fields just because some ids are only unique within run scope.

Scoped identity rules: blocked_episode (object_id=blocked_sequence, resolver scope requires focused_run_id + node membership); scheduler_pass (requires focused_run_id); safe_point (requires focused_run_id); remediation (object_id=remediation_root_id, requires focused_run_id); attempt (object_id=attempt_id, requires focused_run_id).
notes: Small contract, strong resolver. The route contract does not need to grow extra top-level scope ids for each scoped family.

Plans/storage-plan.md — persist refs like resume_url; persist route-adjacent state; stop owning canonical navigation identity
Plans/FileManager.md — keep OpenFile narrow; consume OpenSubject; stop reading path-open as the universal navigation primitive
Plans/Crosswalk.md — declare primitive ownership for route-target / open-subject navigation; declare that storage and surface docs consume, not own, navigation identity

notes: This is the owner-doc adoption map for the routing tranche. Reconcile owner docs in order: Contracts_V0.md, Crosswalk.md, UI_Command_Catalog.md, FinalGUISpec.md, then consumer docs.
